question: MCI vs cognitively normal detection from speech in older adults (P-58: temporal/pause parameters, English and Hungarian clinic samples; P-60: 92 acoustic, prosodic and linguistic features from a Japanese tablet app). Same task and channel; cohorts, language, features and diagnostic criteria differ (allowed).
metric: Accuracy with accuracy (P-60 prints no MCI vs CN AUC in the text). The recorded P-58 '67-92%' is a multi-metric range, not one accuracy.

figures.P-58: Speaker-wise nested LOO-CV, all 15 temporal features, accuracy at the EER threshold: English 84.8% = 28/33, Wilson 69.1-93.3%; Hungarian 75.8% = 25/33, Wilson (p=0.758, z^2/n=0.116, centre=0.731, half-width=0.141) 59.0-87.2%.
figures.P-60: Nested LOO-CV, 46 MCI/43 CN: SVM-RBF on all features 87.6% = 78/89, Wilson (z^2/n=0.043, centre=0.861, half-width=0.069) 79.2-93.0%. Para-linguistic (acoustic + prosodic) features only: MCI vs CN 82.0% (73/89 assumed; Supplementary Table 8 not in the extract), Wilson 72.8-88.6%.

matched_figure_check: P-58's input is temporal/pause parameters only, a para-linguistic input, and P-60 reports MCI vs CN with para-linguistic features only: 82.0% lies inside both P-58 intervals (69.1-93.3%, 59.0-87.2%), and both P-58 values (84.8%, 75.8%) lie inside P-60's 72.8-88.6%. P-58's English all-features 84.8% also agrees with P-60's full 87.6%. Only P-58's Hungarian all-features 75.8% against P-60's full-feature 87.6% crosses (87.6 above 87.2; 75.8 below 79.2; z=1.44), and the matched para-linguistic figure dissolves that gap.
performance_validity: Passes: P-58 best subset 90.9% and P-60 87.6% are below 0.97.
reason: The recorded claim sets P-60's 87.6% against a multi-metric range that contains it. On the papers' printed accuracies, P-58's English cohort agrees with P-60. P-60's own para-linguistic-feature result, the input closest to P-58's, agrees with both P-58 cohorts within uncertainty. The one crossing (P-58 Hungarian all-features against P-60's full model) is dissolved by that matched figure, so the pair fails condition 3.
